cases.groundTruth: Vaughn v. State is reported at 962 P.2d 149 (1998); cited 232 times in corpus.

cases.probe: Bare reporter locator with no caption — exact-key path only.
cases.groundTruth: 962 P.2d 149 is Vaughn v. State (1998).

cases.probe: Vendor/advance-sheet locator for a case that has an official print cite.
cases.groundTruth: 1998 Wyo. LEXIS 97 is a secondary locator for Vaughn v. State; Bluebook form is 962 P.2d 149.
cases.reviewerNote: Key check: if it resolves, correctedCitation must prefer the official reporter, not the vendor form.

cases.input: Thornbury v. Aldenmoor Holdings, LLC, 962 P.2d 149 (1998)
cases.probe: Real locator, fabricated caption — the classic hallucinated-case shape.
cases.groundTruth: 962 P.2d 149 is Vaughn v. State, not Thornbury v. Aldenmoor Holdings.
cases.reviewerNote: A `valid` verdict here is a silent-accept failure — the worst class of error.

cases.probe: Correct case and volume, but an internal pin page given as the first page.
cases.groundTruth: Vaughn v. State begins at page 149, not 152. Page 152 is verified not to be any other case's first page in 962 P.2d.
cases.reviewerNote: If `valid`, correctedCitation must carry the true first page.

cases.probe: Caption of one case pasted onto a real, different case in the same volume.
cases.groundTruth: 962 P.2d 153 is Hodgins v. State (1998), not Vaughn v. State.
cases.reviewerNote: Hardest mismatch shape: both halves exist, only the pairing is wrong. `valid` is a correctness bug.

cases.probe: Correct locator with a wrong year and a foreign-court parenthetical.
cases.groundTruth: Vaughn v. State is a 1998 Wyoming decision, not a 2004 Mont. decision.
cases.reviewerNote: Year/court are part of the citation; endorsing them as `valid` is wrong.

cases.probe: Typo-shaped error: volume digits transposed, caption correct.
cases.groundTruth: Correct locator is 962 P.2d 149. Volume 269 carries no case at page 149 in the corpus.
cases.reviewerNote: Verified: the transposed volume is empty at this page. A name-lookup hedge surfacing the real case is the best answer.

cases.probe: Bluebook R10.9 short form with an internal pin page.
cases.groundTruth: Short form for Vaughn v. State, 962 P.2d 149; pin 153 is inside the opinion.
cases.reviewerNote: A pin in a short form is not an error. `implausible` would be wrong.

cases.probe: Bare `Id.` sent with no antecedent citation in the batch.
cases.groundTruth: Unresolvable in isolation — there is no prior authority to attach it to.
cases.reviewerNote: Must not invent an antecedent. Any affirmative verdict is a hallucination.

cases.input: Vaughn v. State, 962 P.2d 149 (1998); Marbury v. Quillon, 88888 P.2d 9 (2000)
cases.probe: String cite mixing a real authority with a fabricated one.
cases.groundTruth: First unit is real (962 P.2d 149); second is fabricated (volume 88888 does not exist).
cases.reviewerNote: Scored on the primary unit; expansion into >=2 units is asserted separately. The fabricated unit must NOT come back valid.

cases.input: Vaughn v. State, 962 P.2d 149 (1998), aff'd, 999 F.3d 1 (11th Cir. 2001)
cases.probe: Real primary with a fabricated subsequent-history tail.
cases.groundTruth: Primary 962 P.2d 149 is real; 999 F.3d 1 does not exist (F.3d ended at vol. 1000 in 2021, and no such case).
cases.reviewerNote: The history unit should be rejected (not_in_corpus / implausible / not_covered), never valid.

cases.probe: Real, in-force state statute in Bluebook T1.3 form.
cases.groundTruth: Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 1-3-105 is a real provision of Wyoming law.
cases.reviewerNote: Statutes ride the statute ladder, not the reporter corpus. An honest coverage miss is acceptable; invention is not.

cases.probe: Real code name, impossible section number.
cases.groundTruth: No such section exists in the Wyoming code.
cases.reviewerNote: Confirming a nonexistent section as `valid` is a hallucination.

cases.probe: Volume far above the published ceiling for a real reporter series.
cases.groundTruth: P.2d has never reached volume 99999.
cases.reviewerNote: Strong fabrication signal; the ideal answer names it as implausible.

cases.input: Vaughn v. State, 12 Wyo. Sup. Rptr. 4th 88 (1998)
cases.probe: Invented reporter series attached to a real caption.
cases.groundTruth: No reporter named "Wyo. Sup. Rptr. 4th" exists.
cases.reviewerNote: `likely_valid` is acceptable only if candidates are offered without endorsing the fake series.

cases.probe: Westlaw locator with a fabricated WL number.
cases.groundTruth: Vaughn v. State has a print cite (962 P.2d 149); this WL number is invented.
cases.reviewerNote: Vendor IDs are not verifiable from the corpus; do not confirm them.

cases.probe: Authority the corpus flags as no longer good law.
cases.groundTruth: The citation is accurate. McClellan v. Tottenhoff carries good-law status "overruled" with 1 negative treatment(s) in the corpus.
cases.reviewerNote: Citation accuracy and good-law status are separate questions: the cite is correct, so `valid` is the right verdict. The candidate payload must expose goodLaw so the caller sees the negative treatment — that is asserted separately, not via the verdict.

cases.input: see generally the Wyoming cases on this point, passim
cases.probe: Prose with no citation in it.
cases.groundTruth: Contains no citation; nothing to verify.
